keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row (the Mongolian part of 'Turgesh' starts 692). The page gives no area and no map for the first years. Ilterish had 'over 5,000 troops' (Ilterish page) and raided the Tang from 682, attacking Lan Prefecture in 683, so the land is the Tang-facing steppe; Taizong had made the Turks live 'between the Yellow River and Gobi' (639-643). Confidence 1: the page does not place the first camp. Review fix fx-33 (2026-11-01): the Khitan lands (Xar Moron, Laoha, Chaoyang) are subtracted. Second Turkic Khaganate page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Turkic_Khaganate): "In 696-697 Qapaghan subjugated the Khitans"; in 684 the Toquz Oghuz qaghan "had sent letters to the Tang and the Khitans to form an alliance against the Turks", so the Khitans were not Turkic subjects before 696 (the dossier's vassal_start of 697, ledger 3, covers the later relation). The whole Inner Mongolia region reaches 319 cells into the Khitan confederation's land.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe from Qapaghan's accession ('In 692, Qapaghan succeeded his brother as qaghan'). The page gives no area; it describes Qapaghan's frontiers by 'the Tannu Ola, Altai, and Tarbagatai ranges', 'the upper Kerulen to Lake Baikal' and 'the border of Tokharistan'. Cliopatria's 'Turgesh' 692-704 shape (2.87 M km2 on the grid, bbox 87.8-120.7 E, 37.7-52.8 N) fits the first two; the turgesh dossier (ia-01-e) shows it is this khaganate. The Tarbagatai/Tokharistan edge (Dzungaria, Transoxiana) is held only as a vassal tint 711-714 here.

ledger.note: 692: Qapaghan becomes qaghan and the khaganate holds the plateau of Mongolia. 'In 692, Qapaghan succeeded his brother as qaghan.' The pages date no conquest between 685 and 692; Cliopatria's 'Turgesh' 692 shape (the turgesh dossier's Second Turkic Khaganate) starts here, so the step from the Orkhon base to the whole plateau is the bridge (confidence 1).

ledger.note: 696-697: Qapaghan subjugates the Khitans. 'In 696-697 Qapaghan subjugated the Khitans'; the Qapaghan page: 'In the summer of 697, Qapaghan launched another attack on the Khitan's base of operations'.

region.text: the Kyrgyz country beyond the Sayan and Tannu-Ola mountains

ledger.note: 709-710: the Turks crush the Yenisei Kyrgyz. 'in 709-710 the Turks inflicted a crushing defeat on the Yenisei Kyrgyz' (the Qapaghan page: 'subjugating Yenisei Kyrgyz and killing their khagan'). The Kyrgyz homeland (Minusinsk, Tuva) lies at the edge of the Mongolian shape; drawn as a vassal tint.

711: Tonyukuk crushes the Turgesh at the Bolchu river. 'The Battle of Bolchu was fought in 711' in Dzungaria 'close to the Bolchu River' (probably the Ulungur); 'Both Saqal and Zhenu were executed'; the other Onoq leaders submitted.

711: after Bolchu 'all western Turkestan came under the Second Turkic Khaganate'. The Qapaghan page names Tashkent and Ferghana as the lands whose overlord he 'had become'; Temir Kapig in Transoxiana was captured (Tonyukuk inscriptions).

713-714: the Turks fall back from Transoxiana. Tonyukuk's forces fought the Arab army near Samarkand and 'withdrew in 713-714' (Second Turkic page); the Bolchu page: Turkic rule in Transoxiana 'was short-lived, checked by the Arabs'. The Qapaghan page has Kul Tigin's relief of Samarkand defeated in 712.

22 July 716: Qapaghan is killed on his way home from suppressing the Tiele, and the push in the west ends. 'on 22 July 716 ... he was ambushed and killed by Xiezhilue'; the turgesh dossier (ia-01-e) reads 715 and a 714 election of Suluk from other pages; the end year is the death year because none of the five pages opened here dates a Turkic withdrawal from Dzungaria.

744: Kutlug seizes Otuken. 'Kutlug (Kutlug I Bilge Khagan) seized Otuken and beheaded the last Gokturk qaghan, Ozmish Qaghan' after 'an alliance of former subject tribes including the Basmyls, Karluks, and Uyghurs' destroyed the khaganate. The Uyghur dossier has the Basmyls take Otuken first and the Uyghur-Karluk alliance defeat them later in 744.
745: the Khitan tie ends with the khaganate. The pages do not date an earlier end; 'Kulun Beg was beheaded in 745'. Bridging date (confidence 1).
745: the Kyrgyz tie ends with the khaganate. The pages opened here do not date an earlier end. Bridging date (confidence 1).

ledger.note: 745: the last Gokturk khagan is killed. 'Kulun Beg was beheaded in 745' (the infobox and lead end the state in 744); the plateau passes to the Uyghur Khaganate, the Yenisei Kyrgyz take the Sayan country and the Turgesh keep the west.

wars.name: Turkic rebellions against the Tang (679-683)

zones.text: the Tang-facing steppe; raids on Lan Prefecture in 683

wars.outcome: Nishufu (679-680) and Funian (680-681) failed; Ilterish rose in 682, raided Lan Prefecture in 683 and restored the khaganate.
wars.note: Dates of the first two revolts are from the Eastern Turkic Khaganate page.

wars.name: Qapaghan's wars with the Tang
wars.outcome: Raids: Ling Prefecture 694, the Khitan base 697, Dingzhou and Zhao Prefecture in August 698, six crossings of the Yellow River between 693 and 706, Lingwu in 705. The page gives no border change.

wars.name: Battle of Bolchu
wars.outcome: Tonyukuk crushed the Turgesh in 711, killing Saqal and Zhenu; the Turgesh recovered under Suluk.

wars.name: Fall of the Second Turkic Khaganate
wars.outcome: The Basmyls, Karluks and Uyghurs destroyed the khaganate in 744; Kulun Beg was beheaded in 745.
wars.note: The page puts the assassination of Tengri Qaghan in 741.

certainty.note: A steppe khaganate: the pages describe its frontiers by mountain ranges (Tannu Ola, Altai, Tarbagatai), the upper Kerulen and Lake Baikal; no treaty line.

notes: New state: Cliopatria has no Second Turkic Khaganate row; the ia-01-e 'turgesh' notes show that Cliopatria's 'Turgesh' 692-704 (and the Mongolian 75 percent of its 705-749 shapes) is this khaganate, so keyframe 692 points to that shape. The Cliopatria 'Turgesh' 705-749 rows therefore double-draw Mongolia until the Turgesh dossier's correction is applied. Pages disagree on Qapaghan's death: the Qapaghan page says 22 July 716, while the turgesh dossier read 715 from the Second Turkic page; the Bolchu page and the Second Turkic page give 711 for the battle (the Qapaghan page 'dated 711' for Tonyukuk's victory); the turgesh dossier ends the contest in 715. Infobox gives no area. The page gives 744 as the end (infobox and lead) but lists Kulun Beg 744-745; the dossier ends in 745. Counterparts without dossiers: Toquz Oghuz (the Tiele confederation at Otuken, to 744), Khitans (a steppe confederation before the Liao, 696-745 here), Basmyls, Chach and Ferghana. Rulers are not listed because the page's khagan table was not read in full. No wikidata id is given because the page was read through WebFetch only. Gazetteer names used (Inner Mongolia, Orkhon Valley, Tuva, Dzungaria, Chach, Fergana, Liaoxi) all resolve.
